messages.subject: moderation in SEM
parts:
Dear lavaan community,
I am quite new to the field of SEM and wanted to run a moderation analysis. I found various information about the model syntax but basically non about the interpretation of the results. Given one of my models, I get the following results.
I know, that the p-values are to high. However, I would like to understand what would be the meaning of the estimates in case of a p-value < .05
Does the (I) behind SA just indicates a moderating effect of SA on I? And is the -0.180 the effect of SA on R?
Thank you for any advice and help!
Anna

I*SA does not specify a moderation. Rather, SA is assigned the label I. If you want to use product indicators, you must calculate them in advance. For example with indProd (semTools).

parts:
Multi is your new dataset, not a var. You have to change data in sem function.
And you have to create a new var at model 
Like this:
TREINxINST =~ T1.equipe1 + T1.equipe2 + T1.equipe3 + T2.equipe1 + T2.equipe2...

Em ter., 6 de out. de 2020 às 04:53, Anna Schmidt <annasch...@gmail.com> escreveu:
ok, so I tried my best with the indProd function and also found a nice discussion in this forum about it, however, I'm still strugeling and hope for your help.
I first defined the product indicatiors like this:
multi <-indProd(itempar, var1= 1:5, var2 =6, match = FALSE, meanC = TRUE, residualC = FALSE, doubleMC = TRUE, namesProd = NULL)

Given the discussion, I found here: https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/iP4LDqyjlLQ , I thought, I can use the multi variable for the interaction term and thus the moderation effect.
My model is defined like this:

model <- '
  #measurement model
SA =~ par1 +par2 + par3 +par4 + par5

Interaction =~ multi
  #regression formula
R  ~ SF + SA + interaction
'

Unfortunately, R gives me the following error term: lavaan ERROR: missing observed variables in dataset: multi

Thank you in advance!
Anna
